The logs can't tell you which Teams own these Components. The BGL Dataset has no team or owner field. I can tell you which Components have the most FATAL Log Entries, and the answer is very lopsided.

## Observed Facts
Data Scope: BGL Dataset, full time range 2005-06-03 15:42:50 → 2006-01-04 08:00:05 [E2], filtered to `level = FATAL`, grouped by component.

- FATAL Log Entries in total: **855,195** [E1], out of 4,747,963 BGL Log Entries overall [E2].
- By Component (only 4 Components have any FATAL entries [E1]):

| Rank | Component | FATAL Log Entries |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | KERNEL | 626,450 [E1] |
| 2 | APP | 228,536 [E1] |
| 3 | LINKCARD | 206 [E1] |
| 4 | MMCS | 3 [E1] |

- KERNEL and APP together make up nearly all FATAL entries (626,450 + 228,536 out of 855,195 [E1]). LINKCARD and MMCS are minor by comparison.
- These are counts of Log Entries, not incidents. One fault can write many lines.

## Hypotheses
- If BGL follows the usual Blue Gene/L layout, KERNEL would belong to whoever runs compute-node system software or the OS. APP would belong to whoever supports the user jobs and applications that run on the system. LINKCARD would be hardware or interconnect, and MMCS would be the control-system team. This is my guess from what the names usually mean. The logs don't show any of it.

## Unknowns
- **Team ownership.** The available group-by columns for BGL are only `alert_tag`, `component`, `level` and `node` [E2]. No column maps a Component to a Team, so I can't say from the logs who owns KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD or MMCS.
- Whether the large KERNEL and APP counts come from steady repeats or a few bursts. I haven't run a trend query.
- How many distinct incidents these Log Entries represent.

## Next Step
1. **Get ownership from outside the logs.** Check your service catalog, CMDB or on-call roster to map KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD and MMCS to Teams. Start with KERNEL and APP.
2. **Look at KERNEL first.** It has the most FATAL entries by far. I can run a `trend` (by day or week, `level=FATAL`, `component=KERNEL`) to see whether the problem recurs or spikes. I can also group by `alert_tag` and `node` to see whether a few nodes or alert types cause most of it. Then I'd do the same for APP.
